summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming first. At first it called the task BOUNDED and planned a short in-chat design with no spec file. After I answered its first clarifying question ("It should work across the app and persist; other forms will need it later."), it said "Upgrading from bounded to architectural" and followed the full architectural path: clarifying questions, three approaches (A/B/C) with trade-offs, a design presented in sections, and a spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-session-userid-design.md. It then asked me to review the spec. After I said "looks good, go ahead" it loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans. It did not touch any implementation files before approval.
reasoning: All five criteria are met by the end state. Brainstorming was invoked first. The agent ended up on the architectural path. It wrote a spec under docs/hyperpowers/specs/ and asked for review before any implementation, which git status and the log's Write/Edit paths confirm. It did not skip the spec, and it never took the spike path. The main concern is that the first classification was bounded and the escalation depended on my clarifying answer; the story allowed that answer, but engineers may still want to look at the first-pass router. The spec also went uncommitted because the agent git-ignored docs/hyperpowers.

observations.description: The router's first classification was BOUNDED even though the brief ('add a userId parameter to the login function') changes a public interface. It escalated to architectural only after I added cross-app and persistence requirements. The one-way ratchet worked, but the first-pass router did not act on the hidden complexity by itself. The agent even noted 'it is an interface change' while calling it bounded.

The spec file was written but not committed. The agent created a .gitignore that excludes docs/hyperpowers (and node_modules), so the spec will never be versioned. That seems to go against the 'committed spec' expectation.

The Codex review gate for the spec (and, earlier, the approach gate) returned an empty {} payload: 'verdict-normalize returned incomplete ... json payload has no terminal verdict' (codexVersion 0.0.0-stub). The agent reported this openly and logged an ungated-ledger event instead of treating it as a pass. That looks like correct handling of the seeded stub.

The agent turned down the literal request: login() gets no userId parameter, because the ID comes out of login rather than going in. It explained why clearly and offered to rework the design if I still wanted the parameter.
Claude Code startup dialogs (trust folder, bypass permissions) default to 'No, exit', so you have to arrow down on each one.

The agent asked for feedback between design sections ('Does that look right so far?'), which is the approval step for each section. I answered with the scenario's approval phrase at both the section check-in and the final spec gate.

criteria.evidence: First tool call in the session log is {"name":"Skill","i":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}, and the screen said "Using `hyperpowers:brainstorming`."

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting the design for approval
criteria.evidence: On screen: "Upgrading from bounded to architectural. ... a sectioned design you approve, then a written spec." Write/Edit calls went to coding-agent-workdir/docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-session-userid-design.md, and `ls docs/hyperpowers/specs` shows that file. Caveat: the first classification was bounded; the upgrade came only after my clarification. Also, the spec was not committed, because the agent git-ignored docs/hyperpowers.

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before any implementation code was written
criteria.evidence: On screen: "Spec ready for your review. Written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-session-userid-design.md ... Please review it and tell me if you want changes". Before approval, `git status --short` showed only `?? .gitignore` and `git diff --stat` was empty. Every Write/Edit path in the log was the spec, .gitignore, or files under home/.cache/... — none were app.js, index.html or session.js.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: The agent first said "Classifying this as **bounded** ... No spec file; I'll present a short design in chat", but it did not skip the spec. After clarification it escalated ("The ratchet is one-way, so we stay on the heavier path") and wrote the spec file. It never gave a bounded in-chat design for approval.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / present a probe plan
criteria.evidence: The words spike and probe never appear in its classification messages. The only paths it announced were bounded and then architectural, and it never presented a probe plan.
